phase: journal: created by the kernel, then proved to replay after an unclean shutdown
what_this_proves: the data volume now survives a system that ended without warning: 792a wrote a file and never unmounted, and 792b mounted that dirty volume, replayed the journal, and read the file back byte for byte

kernel_log: hfs: mounted RedwoodVar on device xnusys_var

after.journal_header: magic 0x4a4e4c78, start == end, size 8 MiB, at offset 16384

791_journal_created.probe: mount rw -> 0, write 49 -> 49, fsync -> 0, unmount -> 0, remount rw -> 0, read back matched, unmount -> 0

journal_byte_order.what_it_looks_like: on the flash the magic reads 0x784c4e4a, which looks byte-reversed
journal_byte_order.why_it_is_correct: HFS+ journal headers use host byte order, unlike the volume header which is big-endian. The endian field (0x12345678) exists to say which order was used.
journal_byte_order.conclusion: 0x78 0x4c 0x4e 0x4a is the standard ARM64 encoding. Nothing to fix.

792a_dirty_volume.design: mount rw, write 40 bytes, fsync, no unmount; the loader's 420-second return-after ends the system

flash_after.interpretation: start != end, so a transaction was never checkpointed

792a_dirty_volume.kernel_log: no 'Initializing the journal' -- the mount took the journal_open path, not journal_create

792b_replay.design: no writes to the flash first, no fsck, no seed: just mount the dirty volume and read the file
probe_output: before: journal magic=0x4a4e4c78 start=276992 end=355328 not checkpointed
[1] mount rw -> 0   OK -- it mounted a volume that was never unmounted
content = Trial792a: written but never unmounted.
after: journal magic=0x4a4e4c78 start=487424 end=487424 checkpointed
kernel_log: hfs: mounted RedwoodVar on device xnusys_var
792b_replay.the_numbers_line_up: replay_journal replayed from 276992 to 355328, exactly the range 792a left uncommitted
792b_replay.why_it_matters: a volume without a journal refuses a writable mount in this state -- 'cannot mount dirty non-journaled volumes', seen in Trial786c. This one mounted and came back with its data.

a_judgement_that_was_wrong.symptom: fsck.hfsplus -n reported 'invalid primary VHB at 2 result 35' and called the volume corrupt
a_judgement_that_was_wrong.how_it_was_disproved: a fresh volume made by mkfs.hfsplus -v RedwoodVar -b 4096 -J, never mounted, reports exactly the same error
a_judgement_that_was_wrong.conclusion: hfsprogs 540.1 misreports 174 MiB volumes with 4096-byte blocks. The judgement was changed to read the flash and the HLOG directly.
a_judgement_that_was_wrong.side_benefit: the same comparison confirmed every field of our volume header against a reference mkfs -J volume: signature, version, blockSize, totalBlocks, journalInfoBlock, JIB flags/offset/size, and the allocationFile, extentsFile, catalogFile and attributesFile forks all match

a_real_bug_left_alone.symptom: the volume header's modifyDate comes out as 1970-01-01 00:00:21
a_real_bug_left_alone.cause: microtime() returns seconds since boot, not calendar time. The port never reads a platform clock.
code: kern_time.c:243   inittodr() -- 'the calendar has already been set up from the platform clock'
a_real_bug_left_alone.impact: volume and file timestamps read 1970; macOS would call the volume damaged. Mount, write, unmount and journal replay do not depend on timestamps.
a_real_bug_left_alone.how_to_fix: mtkloader.c:212 already mentions an epoch= kernel argument in a comment, but neither the loader nor the kernel implements it. It would need a time source in the loader, the argument on the command line, PE_parse_boot_argn("epoch") in the kernel, and one call to clock_set_calendar_microtime().
a_real_bug_left_alone.not_done_because: it is independent of the journal work and would mean touching the loader

786.bug: the driver silently refused any write not aligned to 4096, and HFS Plus writes its volume header in 512-byte pieces
786.fix: read the block, lay the given bytes over the part they cover, write the whole block back
786.proof: f_bfree moved 41447 -> 41446; host test test-rmw.c passes 211 checks

788-790.bug: the driver called buf_map() and never buf_unmap(), leaking a UPL reference per file I/O; vclean() then waited forever in vm_object_paging_wait
788-790.fix: buf_unmap before buf_biodone on every path that mapped; removed a duplicate buf_map in the write branch
788-790.proof: the same probe that hung for 420 s in 785c returned 0 in 788

not_done: mounting at /private/var itself -- the probes mount at /private/var/tmp/<name>
the directory skeleton a real /private/var needs (mobile, root, db, keychains, run, tmp) with their owners and modes
xnusys_hfsseed still cannot read its writes back -- it reads through /dev/rxnusys, a character node bounded by the APFS container
